name: BMW Z4 M Coupe (E86)
engine: 3.2L S54B32 naturally-aspirated inline-six with individual throttle bodies
torque: 262 lb-ft @ 4,900 rpm (US SAE; Euro cars rated 343 PS / 269 lb-ft)
reliability: 8/10 — the E86 Z4 M Coupe is the hard-top 'clownshoe' shooting-brake sharing the E46 M3's high-revving S54 straight-six, and the fixed roof makes it stiffer and sharper than the M Roadster. The S54's headline concern is rod-bearing wear (potentially catastrophic, so interval replacement is the accepted practice) along with VANOS wear and the usual aging cooling system — though the Z4 M is generally viewed as less bearing-troubled than the earliest 2001–2003 E46 M3s. Low production and a cult shape make a well-maintained one a genuine modern collectible.
cost_to_own: Insurance: High (rare two-seat M) · Maintenance ~$1,500/yr with rod bearings and VANOS as the budgeted big items · Rising collector interest — clean, documented cars appreciate
popular_mods: Preventive rod-bearing replacement — the essential S54 insurance job
A VANOS rebuild to restore response and quiet the rattle
A cooling-system refresh (water pump, thermostat, radiator, expansion tank)
A quality suspension/alignment refresh to sharpen the already-stiff coupe
Honest take: spend on the rod bearings, VANOS, and cooling before anything cosmetic — that's what protects a rising-value S54 car

generations.Z4 M Coupe (2006–2008, E86): The fixed-roof, shooting-brake derivative of the Z4 roadster, powered by the E46 M3's S54 straight-six. The hard top adds real chassis rigidity, making it a sharp, communicative driver's car now prized as a modern collectible.
generations.Z4 M Roadster (E85): The open-top sibling shared the S54 drivetrain but with less structural stiffness; the coupe is the enthusiast and collector favorite.

common_issues: S54 rod-bearing wear — can be catastrophic; interval replacement is the accepted practice
VANOS unit failure — rattle, worn seals, and oil-pressure loss
Aging cooling-system components (water pump, thermostat, expansion tank)
Differential and rear-subframe stress on hard-used cars
Sensitivity to infrequent oil changes given the high-strung S54
maintenance_tips: Replace the rod bearings on interval — treat it as scheduled maintenance, not a repair
Service the VANOS at the first sign of rattle or lost response
Refresh the cooling system proactively on any car with unknown history
Use the correct 10W-60 M-spec synthetic and change it on the shorter interval
Buy on documented service history — a maintained S54 is worth the premium
